record.paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
record.original_question: Construct a quaternionic Weyl algebra H[x, partial] with suitable variables x and differential operators partial. The construction must handle noncommutativity both in quaternionic coefficients and in variables, and it should be usable for systems of differential equations in the sense that the spaces R(U) of regular functions and F(U) of quaternionic hyperfunctions can be treated as modules over an algebra A_1(H).

evidence.quote: Problem: Construct a quaternionic Weyl algebra.
we have, apparently, a double non commutativity in both the coefficients and the variables.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the (noncommutative) skew field of quaternions, with basis $1,i,j,k$ satisfying $i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1$. For an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb{H}^n$, let $\mathcal{R}(U)$ denote the space of (left) Cauchy–Fueter regular functions $f:U	o\mathbb{H}$, i.e. smooth functions annihilated by each Cauchy–Fueter operator
$$\overline{\partial}_\ell =  rac{\partial}{\partial x_0^{(\ell)}} + i rac{\partial}{\partial x_1^{(\ell)}} + j rac{\partial}{\partial x_2^{(\ell)}} + k rac{\partial}{\partial x_3^{(\ell)}},\qquad \ell=1,\dots,n,$$
and let $\mathcal{F}(U)$ denote the corresponding space of quaternionic hyperfunctions on $U$.

Construct an associative $\mathbb{R}$-algebra $A_1(\mathbb{H})=\mathbb{H}[x,\partial]$, called the quaternionic Weyl algebra, generated by quaternionic ``variables'' $x_1,\dots,x_n$ and quaternionic ``derivations'' $\partial_1,\dots,\partial_n$ together with quaternionic scalar coefficients, such that:

(i) the algebra correctly encodes the double noncommutativity inherent in the situation, namely the noncommutativity of the quaternionic coefficients and the noncommutativity between the variables and the differential operators;

(ii) the algebra acts naturally on $\mathcal{R}(U)$ and on $\mathcal{F}(U)$, endowing each of them with the structure of an $A_1(\mathbb{H})$-module;

(iii) the algebra is suitable for the algebraic analysis of overdetermined systems of linear differential equations with quaternionic coefficients in the sense of Ehrenpreis–Palamodov, so that homological methods (resolutions, syzygies, Ext-modules) can be developed within it.

Give an explicit construction of $A_1(\mathbb{H})$ with these properties, establish its basic structural properties (e.g. defining relations, a PBW-type basis, filtration and associated graded ring, Noetherianity, global dimension), and verify that $\mathcal{R}(U)$ and $\mathcal{F}(U)$ are naturally $A_1(\mathbb{H})$-modules.
artifact.status_search_result: A construction called "the quaternionic Weyl algebra" $A_1(\mathbb{H})$ has been introduced and its main properties studied, with examples of $A_1(\mathbb{H})$-modules useful for resolving systems of differential equations whose operators lie in $A_1(\mathbb{H})$ (see Colombo–Damiano–Sabadini–Struppa, "On the quaternionic Weyl algebra", Adv. Appl. Clifford Algebras). The general program of using such an algebra to systematically analyze the Cauchy–Fueter system in several variables is, however, still being developed, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On the quaternionic Weyl algebra - Advances in Applied Clifford Algebras
status_evidence.snippet: A notion of quaternionic Weyl algebra A_1(H) is introduced and its main properties are studied. Examples of A_1(H)-modules are given which are useful in the resolution of systems of differential equations whose linear differential operators are in A_1(H).
status_evidence.claim: A quaternionic Weyl algebra A_1(H) has been constructed and its module theory developed for use in systems of differential equations, addressing the construction problem at least partially.

status_evidence.title: Regular functions of several quaternionic variables and the Cauchy-Fueter complex
status_evidence.snippet: Regular functions in several variables are infinitely differentiable functions satisfying an overdetermined system of differential equations; algebraic approach following Ehrenpreis.
status_evidence.claim: R(U) is studied as a module over an algebra of differential operators in the Cauchy–Fueter setting.
